method: Saturday provisional contest proposals (Andy approved in chat ~6:10 pm PT): locked contest line vs Bookmaker 5:43 pm PT, baseline fair line, ESPN injury feed and reviewed expert/media intake. Named expert picks are context. Friday entries are in the .bak file. Margin-sim expected points (win + half a push; pipeline-standard double shrink) and an FTN matchup-analytics sensitivity from reports/intel/w11-model/sim-w11-sat.json were added Saturday 8:21 pm PT; no pick was re-ranked.

pitch.text: The contest gives Tampa Bay +7, while Bookmaker moved from DET -6 Thursday to DET -3.5 at 5:43 pm. That is 3.5 points of contest value, the most on the slate. The margin sim makes TB +7 the best contest side on the slate: 0.597 expected points (0.617 on the FTN matchup analytics), winning 56.9% and pushing 5.5%.
Doug Kezirian named TB +7 his second favorite bet on the Action Network podcast, and Ben Fawkes reported sharp sportsbook action on the Bucs at +7 and +6.5.

pushback.text: CAVEAT: Mayfield Questionable (foot/plantar fascia and thumb). Bowles said only that he is trending toward starting; if rookie Jalon Daniels starts instead, the 3.5-point value case collapses.
Tampa Bay is without S Antoine Winfield Jr., and the baseline fair line still makes Detroit a 4.6-point favorite, so the model edge on +7 is 2.4 points rather than the full 3.5 against market.

pitch.text: The contest gives Tennessee +8, while Bookmaker is at TEN +7. The extra point runs through 7, the second key number. The fair line is DAL -7.8.
Dallas is missing CB DaRon Bland, TE Jake Ferguson, WR Jonathan Mingo, S P.J. Locke and G Tyler Booker. Andrew Erickson backed TEN +8.5, and Ben Fawkes reported sharp action on the Titans at +8.

pushback.text: Tennessee's pass defense ranks last in the NFL (xEP Network rates Dak Prescott's matchup 100/100), and RB Tyjae Spears went to IR on Saturday, concentrating the backfield on Tony Pollard.

62% of BetMGM money was on Dallas -7.5 (John Ewing), and BetOnline already offers TEN +9 at -125, so the contest number is not unique in the market. The margin sim rates TEN +8 at 0.523 expected points, fourth on the slate but only slightly above even; the case leans on sharp and expert support.

pitch.text: The baseline fair line is LAC +0.2, so the contest NYJ +3.5 carries a 3.7-point model edge and the half point through 3 that the books (LAC -3) do not offer. The margin sim rates NYJ +3.5 at 0.555 expected points, second on the slate, and the FTN matchup analytics agree (0.562).

The Chargers' secondary is short: S Kendall Williamson and CB Rodney Shelley are out, and CBs Tarheeb Still and Isas Waxter are questionable, leaving up to 4 of the defensive backs limited or missing.

pushback.text: The Jets are without WRs Omar Cooper Jr. and Isaiah Williams (2 receivers out), and Geno Smith was only cleared from an ankle issue on Friday, two days before kickoff.
75% of BetMGM money was on the Chargers -3 (John Ewing), and the Jets travel three time zones to the West Coast, so the public and the travel spot both lean against New York.

pitch.text: The contest has SF -3, while Bookmaker and BetOnline are at -3.5. The contest number wins on a field-goal margin, and the fair line is SF -5. The margin sim rates SF -3 at 0.536 expected points, third on the slate, with a 8.2% push chance on exactly 3.
The SGPN on-air recap backed SF -3, and Kendra Middleton nominated SF -3.5 on her contest card. Favorites are 39-25 ATS in NFL international games (John Ewing).

pushback.text: San Francisco is without WR Brandon Aiyuk, WR Mike Evans is questionable, and Kirk Cousins threw for 207 yards and 2 TDs in his Week 10 return.
The 49ers were the most-bet side at BetMGM (76% of money on -3). Mexico City altitude and a 61% rain chance add variance.

pitch.text: The contest gives Denver -10, half a point better than Bookmaker (-10.5) at 5:43 pm PT, so a 10-point Broncos win is a push here instead of a loss at the book.
Doug Kezirian (first favorite bet), Lock & Cash and the SGPN recap all backed Denver at -10 or -9.5, and Ben Fawkes reported sharp action at -9 and -9.5.

pushback.text: The baseline fair line is DEN -8.9, so the model sides with Las Vegas at +10. Kendra Middleton disclosed a personal bet on the Raiders +10.5. The margin sim rates DEN -10 at 0.494 expected points, below even in both views (0.472 analytics), and prefers Las Vegas +10.
TE Brock Bowers and K Matt Gay are both questionable for Las Vegas; if either plays, the Raiders keep a late-score path that raises the backdoor-cover risk on a 10-point spread.
